newsitem.title: FRANCE: France, Germany fail to agree on EU jobs plan.
newsitem.headline: France, Germany fail to agree on EU jobs plan.

text.p: France and Germany failed to agree on a European Union initiative to promote economic growth and jobs on Friday but both sides pledged to work together to seek an accord in Amsterdam next week.

New French Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said the EU should revive an agreement reached in Essen, Germany, in 1994 to launch a major labour-intensive public works programme but German Chancellor Helmut Kohl opposed any new spending.

Kohl said he had only received French proposals for an EU initiative on growth and jobs to complement a pact on limiting budget deficits on Thursday night and could not take a final position on it. French and German experts would work on the question intensively before a meeting of EU finance ministers on Sunday and the Amsterdam summit next Monday and Tuesday.
The chancellor said whatever was agreed must not reopen the so-called stability pact or involve new funds or new powers for the European Commission.

"It seems to us...that an important decision of principle was taken in Essen on infrastructure programmes. After that, it is a matter of the political will," Jospin said. "Past decisions can be the basis for action now."

Kohl replied that the most important factor in fighting record unemployment in Europe was changing mentalities and becoming competitive, adding: "I don't approve of trying to spend the same money twice."
But both leaders, at a joint news conference with French President Jacques Chirac, said they were optimistic that a solution would be found at the Amsterdam summit.
